title: Ode to Joy
_about: Beethoven's tune (Symphony No. 9, 1824) in the four-part hymn setting from the Mutopia Project (public domain, typeset by Peter Chubb, Mutopia-2009/08/05-528), transposed from G to C. Melody and alto are at written pitch; tenor and bass are moved up into the bells' lower octave (C5-C6), so the chords are Beethoven's but the low voices sit closer together than in the score. SIMPLIFIED for the 15 bells: (1) the alto, tenor and bass leave out their eighth notes (each dotted-quarter-plus-eighth becomes a half note), and a note they repeat within a bar is rung once and held, as handbell choirs often do; (2) four chromatic notes have no bell and are replaced by a chord tone: alto C# in bar 12 (held E), bass D# in bar 11 (B), tenor and bass F-natural in bar 13 (F# and A, making it a plain dominant chord), named in the G-major score. In bars 9, 10 and 12 the tenor's high G keeps the line moving by step instead of leaping a seventh. The melody is complete. One beat = a quarter note.

_arrangements: 2 phones: melody only. 3 phones: melody and bass. 4 phones: all four voices of the hymn, which is also what the Demo plays. Notes on two phones take turns ('alternate'): each time, the note goes to a holder that is not already ringing another note of that chord, idle longest first.
